## Claim being audited

This is a fresh-tablet construction plan for all ten configured claims. The manuscript naturally decomposes into three branches: (A) fronts, locally constant multi-sequences, and Nash-Williams; (B) generalized shifts on increasing self-embeddings of the naturals; and (C) the iterated nonempty powerset and its hereditarily countable part. There is no defect in the paper that prevents formalization, but branch C must preserve the paper's genuinely iterated, well-founded hierarchy rather than silently replacing it by the first-level type `Set Q`.

## Foundational interfaces

Use Mathlib's unbundled `WellQuasiOrdered r` for the paper's sequence definition of wqo, with an explicit `IsPreorder` assumption on `r` when order laws are needed. Represent an infinite subset of the naturals by an increasing order embedding `IncSeq := Nat ↪o Nat`. This single type also represents the paper's monoid `IIf`; composition is the monoid action, and shift is right-composition with successor. Define finite-prefix agreement and `LocallyConstant` directly: a value at `x` is decided by some finite prefix of `x`. This is equivalent to continuity into a discrete type in the Baire subspace topology, but keeps all combinatorial proofs independent of general topology. State and prove closure under composition and restriction early.

For fronts, use the paper's explicit definition (paper lines 1078-1090), over finite strictly increasing lists or an equivalent finite-set-with-prefix representation. A `Front X` must carry a prefix-free family and the density/bar property against every subsequence of the base `X`, including the exceptional trivial front `{empty}`. Define restriction to a subsequence, rays, the prefix tree, sub-front, super-sequence, and the shift relation on finite members. Prove uniqueness of the front member that is a proper prefix of an infinite sequence, restriction remains a front, rays remain fronts, and the prefix tree is well-founded. The Nash-Williams proof can then recurse on accessibility in this tree; an explicit ordinal-valued rank is not needed. Its fusion step also needs the elementary infinite pigeonhole lemma for a Boolean sequence.

For topological digraphs, use a small structure or predicate for a prefix-continuous relation homomorphism. Define continuous-homomorphic reducibility, `BetterRel r` as absence of a prefix-continuous homomorphism from shift into the complement of `r`, and `GBetter g r` analogously with right-composition by `g`. Define `Bqo r` by the paper's equivalent bad locally constant multi-sequence clause (lines 1445-1459), and later prove the super-sequence equivalence rather than taking it as a second definition.

For the full hierarchy, use a universe-polymorphic tagged PSet-style inductive type: an atom `q : Q`, or a nonempty family of earlier trees indexed by an arbitrary small type. Define the lifted relation by exactly the four clauses at paper lines 1404-1419. Raw well-founded tree codes may be used instead of an extensional quotient because mutually extensional codes are equivalent in this quasi-order, but that equivalence and invariance must be proved. Define hereditary countability recursively by countability of every node's index type. This preserves arbitrary well-founded iteration; `Set Q` is reserved for the separate first-powerset Rado theorem.

## Intended DAG

```text
IncSeq + prefix/local constancy + WQO
  |-- orbit/block arithmetic --> RmapLemma + EmapLemma --> MainProp
  |                                               |--> g-BQO --> lines 1748-1753
  |-- Front core --> restriction/ray/tree-WF --> NashWilliams
  |                                      |--> finite-color front theorem --> SuperNW
  |                                      |--> fixed-arity Ramsey (n=3,4) --> Rado embedding
  |-- Front core + local constancy --> super/multi bridge --+
  |                                                         + NashWilliams --> perfect/bad dichotomy --> subarr
  |-- Bqo core + iterated Power tree/order/game --> bad-map reflection --> PowerQPresBqo
                                                        |
  Front tree-WF + bad-super bridge --> ConverseGame ----+--> HerCtblWqo
  HerCtbl countable-node closure + WQO/WF lemmas ------------> HerCtblWellF
```

The generalized-shift branch should split `RmapLemma` from `EmapLemma`. For nonidentity `g`, first prove the least moved point exists, all smaller points are fixed, every increasing injection satisfies `n <= f n`, and the orbit `G(n)=g^[n](k_g)` is strictly increasing and unbounded. `RmapLemma` is restriction along `G`. For `EmapLemma`, isolate the unique orbit-block decomposition and prove separately that the paper's piecewise sigma is increasing, prefix-continuous, and satisfies `sigma(f after succ)=sigma(f) after g` (paper lines 1787-1835). `MainProp` is then just the pair of homomorphisms.

Nash-Williams should be proved before developing any independent infinite Ramsey library. The fixed-length fronts give exactly the homogeneous triple and quadruple instances used in the proof of the target at lines 985-987. For that target, separately define Rado's order, domination on `Set Q`, bad sequences of pairs, the witness-selection lemma from a bad powerset sequence, and the two thinning lemmas. The final map must reflect as well as preserve Rado's order; proving only monotonicity is insufficient.

The multi-sequence branch should construct the minimal deciding front of a locally constant finite coloring (paper lines 1277-1289), apply Nash-Williams, and obtain the perfect-versus-bad dichotomy specialized to shift. This is enough for all three implications in `lem:subarr`; do not record only the one implication written out at lines 1660-1662. In particular, prove transport of badness and perfectness through the super/multi correspondence and through restriction.

The powerset-preservation node must sit above a substantive reflection theorem matching paper lines 1533-1550: a bad locally constant map into the full iterated hierarchy yields a bad locally constant map into the atoms. Build the finite descending comparison game, prove termination from structural well-foundedness, prove the four-clause order is equivalent to a winning strategy for player II and its negation to one for player I, then formalize the diagonal copying construction. Do not introduce the final preservation theorem until these interfaces have complete natural-language proofs.

For `HerCtblQ`, prove both directions in paper lines 1585-1590. Forward uses powerset preservation, bqo implies wqo, and heredity to the countable subtype. Reverse uses a bad super-sequence, well-founded recursion on its front tree to form the countably branching `tilde f`, and `ConverseGame`. For the well-founded characterization, one direction is Mathlib's wqo-implies-well-founded strict part. The converse is special to `HerCtblQ`: from a bad sequence, form the countable nonempty nodes of its successive tails and obtain a strict descending chain. Do not use the false general statement that every well-founded preorder is wqo.

## Target order

Reach targets in this order: (1) `MainProp`; (2) `g-BQO`; (3) `lines:1748-1753`; (4) `cor:NashWill`; (5) `corollary:SuperNW`; (6) `lem:subarr`; (7) `lines:985-987`; (8) `cor PowerQPresBqo`; (9) `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`; (10) `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The first three give an early, relatively independent closed branch. Nash-Williams then supplies both the front results and the finite Ramsey thinning used by Laver's theorem. The iterated-powerset results come last because their game/reflection infrastructure is the deepest part of the manuscript.

Each mathematical concept above should be its own paired node; do not stack helper claims in one ordinary `.tex` file. Every proof-bearing node needs a complete proof block, and dependencies should cite principal nodes only. Keep imports above the tablet marker and the unique `-- BODY` marker immediately after the principal declaration's body delimiter.

This is the cycle-5 coverage re-plan for the five configured targets that still have no covering node. The first four tasks of the prior plan are complete: the increasing-embedding/local-constancy foundation, generalized-shift reduction and consequences, and the front/Nash-Williams/SuperNW statement package are present. Their configured targets are covered and should not be reconstructed. The current node-level correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness findings on that already-built material are separate verifier work; this coverage plan uses the principal statements and follows the reviewer's instruction not to rewrite them during the next construction burst.

The remaining targets are exactly `lem:subarr`, `lines:985-987`, `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The four still-live tasks from the prior plan remain mathematically correct, but they now need sharper attachment points and smaller support packages.

## Existing interfaces and one correction

`IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `Bqo` provide the multi-sequence side. `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `NashWilliams`, and `SuperNW` provide the front side. The probe at `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-5-request-33/right_comp_probe.lean` confirms on the nontrivial embedding `n |-> 2*n` that `ShiftMap x` evaluates as `x (n+1)`, so the existing shift interface can be reused.

There is, however, an orientation issue relevant to the later hereditary-countability construction. The current Lean signature of `FrontTreeWellFounded` makes `u` related to `v` when `u` is a proper initial segment of `v`. In Lean's `WellFounded r` recursion, computing at `s` may call values at `t` when `r t s`; the paper's definition of `TildeF(s)` at lines 1559-1563 calls `TildeF(t)` for strict extensions `t` of `s`. Thus that construction needs the converse relation, `r child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. Add a correctly oriented helper for this use; do not pretend the current signature supplies the recursion principle. This does not require changing the already covered Nash-Williams statement during the next burst.

## Remaining DAG

```text
Front + SuperSequence + ProperPrefixSet
  + IncSeq/RightComp + LocallyConstant
    -> unique front selector / super extension
    -> minimal deciding front / multi restriction
    -> finite shift and bad/perfect transports
    + NashWilliams -> shift perfect-or-bad dichotomy -> Subarr

NashWilliams -> constant-k front Ramsey (k=3,4)
  + Rado order + domination on Set Q
  + bad-powerset witness map -> two thinnings -> RadoEmbedding

PowerTree(atom, arbitrary nonempty indexed node)
  -> support + four-clause PowerRel + preorder/extensional invariance
  -> finite comparison strategies and canonical negative moves
  + LocallyConstant/BadMultiSequence -> BadMapReflection
  + Bqo -> PowerQPresBqo

PowerTree + HereditarilyCountable
  + correctly oriented front-extension well-foundedness
  + bad multi-to-super transport -> TildeF -> ConverseGame
  + PowerQPresBqo + Bqo-to-Wqo -> BqoHerCtblWqo
  + countable tail-node construction -> BqoHerCtblWellF
```

For `lem:subarr`, represent a sub-multi-sequence of `h` by precomposition with `RightComp z`. Prove its commutation with `ShiftMap`, preservation of local constancy, and preservation of badness. For a super-sequence on an arbitrary front base `X`, select the unique front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration whose range lies in `X`; reindex through an increasing enumeration of `X` when a global `MultiSequence` is required. The minimal deciding-front construction of paper lines 1277-1289 then makes the Boolean coloring `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))` into a super-sequence. `NashWilliams` yields a restriction on which this coloring is constant, hence a perfect-or-bad dichotomy. The target node must state all three equivalent clauses at paper lines 1652-1658 and prove every implication, including both badness transports and perfectness under restriction.

For `lines:985-987`, use a first-level domination relation on `Set Q`; this is intentionally separate from the iterated hierarchy. Define Rado pairs with `m<n` and the two-clause Rado order. From failure of wqo for domination, choose the bad pair-indexed witness map from paper lines 957-980. Obtain the homogeneous triple and quadruple sets from `NashWilliams` applied to constant-cardinality fronts, as required by process memory pm-0003. The final theorem assumes that `r` is a quasi-order and wqo, and produces a relation embedding of Rado's order into `r`. Its proof must establish both preservation and reflection; the three reflection cases at paper line 993 use badness and transitivity and may not be replaced by monotonicity alone.

For `cor PowerQPresBqo`, retain process memory pm-0002. The carrier must be a universe-polymorphic well-founded tree/preset type with an atom constructor for `Q` and a constructor for an arbitrary nonempty indexed family of earlier trees. Define the lifted relation by all four cases at paper lines 1404-1419, including the often-omitted set-to-atom universal clause. Raw presentations are acceptable only after proving that duplicate/extensional presentations are mutually related and that all predicates used by the targets are invariant under that equivalence. The comparison game, or an equivalent inductively defined negative strategy, must expose the existential Player-I choices supplied by `not PowerRel`. Canonicalize choices as functions of the compared tree values: choosing unrelated strategies separately for each input `x` would not prove that the reflected atom map is locally constant. The reflection node must match lines 1533-1550: every bad locally constant map into the full hierarchy yields a bad locally constant atom-valued map whose value lies in the source support. `PowerQPresBqo` is then the immediate contradiction with `Bqo r`.

For the hereditary targets, define hereditary countability recursively: atoms qualify, and a node qualifies exactly when its index type is countable and every child qualifies. Prove closure under nonempty countable families and induced-subtype inheritance. The reverse direction of `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` uses the bad multi-to-super bridge, the correctly oriented front recursion to build `TildeF`, and the comparison-game copying lemma `ConverseGame`; every internal node of `TildeF` is indexed by a subset of `Nat`, hence is hereditarily countable. The forward direction uses `PowerQPresBqo`, restriction to the hereditary subtype, and the elementary theorem that bqo implies wqo.

Finally, `thm BqoHerCtblWellF` must use the special closure of this hierarchy, not the false general assertion that a well-founded quasi-order is wqo. Wqo implies well-foundedness of the strict part. Conversely, from a bad sequence `(a_n)` in the hereditary hierarchy, form the nonempty countable tail nodes `A_n = {a_k | n <= k}`. Then `A_(n+1) <= A_n`, while `A_n <= A_(n+1)` would compare `a_n` with some later `a_k`, contradicting badness. These tail nodes give a strict descending chain inside the same hereditary hierarchy.

Proceed in this order: (1) the super/multi bridge and `Subarr`; (2) constant-arity Ramsey support and the Rado embedding; (3) the iterated hierarchy core and bad-map reflection, then `PowerQPresBqo`; (4) hereditary countability, `TildeF`, and `ConverseGame`; (5) the wqo and well-founded hereditary characterizations. Each helper is its own paired node, dependencies cite principal declarations only, and every new proof-bearing TeX node must contain a complete proof rather than `SKETCH:`.

audit_plan.report:
## Claim being audited

This is the cycle-5 coverage re-plan for the five configured targets that still have no covering node. The first four tasks of the prior plan are complete: the increasing-embedding/local-constancy foundation, generalized-shift reduction and consequences, and the front/Nash-Williams/SuperNW statement package are present. Their configured targets are covered and should not be reconstructed. The current node-level correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness findings on that already-built material are separate verifier work; this coverage plan uses the principal statements and follows the reviewer's instruction not to rewrite them during the next construction burst.

The remaining targets are exactly `lem:subarr`, `lines:985-987`, `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The four still-live tasks from the prior plan remain mathematically correct, but they now need sharper attachment points and smaller support packages.

## Existing interfaces and one correction

`IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `Bqo` provide the multi-sequence side. `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `NashWilliams`, and `SuperNW` provide the front side. The probe at `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-5-request-33/right_comp_probe.lean` confirms on the nontrivial embedding `n |-> 2*n` that `ShiftMap x` evaluates as `x (n+1)`, so the existing shift interface can be reused.

There is, however, an orientation issue relevant to the later hereditary-countability construction. The current Lean signature of `FrontTreeWellFounded` makes `u` related to `v` when `u` is a proper initial segment of `v`. In Lean's `WellFounded r` recursion, computing at `s` may call values at `t` when `r t s`; the paper's definition of `TildeF(s)` at lines 1559-1563 calls `TildeF(t)` for strict extensions `t` of `s`. Thus that construction needs the converse relation, `r child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. Add a correctly oriented helper for this use; do not pretend the current signature supplies the recursion principle. This does not require changing the already covered Nash-Williams statement during the next burst.

## Remaining DAG

```text
Front + SuperSequence + ProperPrefixSet
  + IncSeq/RightComp + LocallyConstant
    -> unique front selector / super extension
    -> minimal deciding front / multi restriction
    -> finite shift and bad/perfect transports
    + NashWilliams -> shift perfect-or-bad dichotomy -> Subarr

NashWilliams -> constant-k front Ramsey (k=3,4)
  + Rado order + domination on Set Q
  + bad-powerset witness map -> two thinnings -> RadoEmbedding

PowerTree(atom, arbitrary nonempty indexed node)
  -> support + four-clause PowerRel + preorder/extensional invariance
  -> finite comparison strategies and canonical negative moves
  + LocallyConstant/BadMultiSequence -> BadMapReflection
  + Bqo -> PowerQPresBqo

PowerTree + HereditarilyCountable
  + correctly oriented front-extension well-foundedness
  + bad multi-to-super transport -> TildeF -> ConverseGame
  + PowerQPresBqo + Bqo-to-Wqo -> BqoHerCtblWqo
  + countable tail-node construction -> BqoHerCtblWellF
```

For `lem:subarr`, represent a sub-multi-sequence of `h` by precomposition with `RightComp z`. Prove its commutation with `ShiftMap`, preservation of local constancy, and preservation of badness. For a super-sequence on an arbitrary front base `X`, select the unique front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration whose range lies in `X`; reindex through an increasing enumeration of `X` when a global `MultiSequence` is required. The minimal deciding-front construction of paper lines 1277-1289 then makes the Boolean coloring `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))` into a super-sequence. `NashWilliams` yields a restriction on which this coloring is constant, hence a perfect-or-bad dichotomy. The target node must state all three equivalent clauses at paper lines 1652-1658 and prove every implication, including both badness transports and perfectness under restriction.

For `lines:985-987`, use a first-level domination relation on `Set Q`; this is intentionally separate from the iterated hierarchy. Define Rado pairs with `m<n` and the two-clause Rado order. From failure of wqo for domination, choose the bad pair-indexed witness map from paper lines 957-980. Obtain the homogeneous triple and quadruple sets from `NashWilliams` applied to constant-cardinality fronts, as required by process memory pm-0003. The final theorem assumes that `r` is a quasi-order and wqo, and produces a relation embedding of Rado's order into `r`. Its proof must establish both preservation and reflection; the three reflection cases at paper line 993 use badness and transitivity and may not be replaced by monotonicity alone.

For `cor PowerQPresBqo`, retain process memory pm-0002. The carrier must be a universe-polymorphic well-founded tree/preset type with an atom constructor for `Q` and a constructor for an arbitrary nonempty indexed family of earlier trees. Define the lifted relation by all four cases at paper lines 1404-1419, including the often-omitted set-to-atom universal clause. Raw presentations are acceptable only after proving that duplicate/extensional presentations are mutually related and that all predicates used by the targets are invariant under that equivalence. The comparison game, or an equivalent inductively defined negative strategy, must expose the existential Player-I choices supplied by `not PowerRel`. Canonicalize choices as functions of the compared tree values: choosing unrelated strategies separately for each input `x` would not prove that the reflected atom map is locally constant. The reflection node must match lines 1533-1550: every bad locally constant map into the full hierarchy yields a bad locally constant atom-valued map whose value lies in the source support. `PowerQPresBqo` is then the immediate contradiction with `Bqo r`.

For the hereditary targets, define hereditary countability recursively: atoms qualify, and a node qualifies exactly when its index type is countable and every child qualifies. Prove closure under nonempty countable families and induced-subtype inheritance. The reverse direction of `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` uses the bad multi-to-super bridge, the correctly oriented front recursion to build `TildeF`, and the comparison-game copying lemma `ConverseGame`; every internal node of `TildeF` is indexed by a subset of `Nat`, hence is hereditarily countable. The forward direction uses `PowerQPresBqo`, restriction to the hereditary subtype, and the elementary theorem that bqo implies wqo.

Finally, `thm BqoHerCtblWellF` must use the special closure of this hierarchy, not the false general assertion that a well-founded quasi-order is wqo. Wqo implies well-foundedness of the strict part. Conversely, from a bad sequence `(a_n)` in the hereditary hierarchy, form the nonempty countable tail nodes `A_n = {a_k | n <= k}`. Then `A_(n+1) <= A_n`, while `A_n <= A_(n+1)` would compare `a_n` with some later `a_k`, contradicting badness. These tail nodes give a strict descending chain inside the same hereditary hierarchy.

## Work order

Proceed in this order: (1) the super/multi bridge and `Subarr`; (2) constant-arity Ramsey support and the Rado embedding; (3) the iterated hierarchy core and bad-map reflection, then `PowerQPresBqo`; (4) hereditary countability, `TildeF`, and `ConverseGame`; (5) the wqo and well-founded hereditary characterizations. Each helper is its own paired node, dependencies cite principal declarations only, and every new proof-bearing TeX node must contain a complete proof rather than `SKETCH:`.

ops.body: The recursion at paper lines 1559-1563 defines `TildeF(s)` using `TildeF(t)` for strict extensions `t` of `s`. In Lean, `WellFounded r` permits a recursive call from `s` to `t` when `r t s`; therefore the required relation is `r child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. A theorem whose relation is instead `r shorter longer` has the opposite orientation and cannot justify this recursion, even though that relation is trivially well-founded by decreasing finite-set cardinality. Add or repair an extension-oriented well-foundedness theorem before constructing `TildeF`.
